The samples are allowed to harden for 2-hours, which they are removed from the jig utilizing the specimen removal set screw. The lap shear specimens are then allowed to complete curing for 24 hours in a controlled environment (23 C at 50%rH). The product technical data sheet describes curing the adhesive at elevated temperatures, although this was not followed as it was a concern for the polymer composite within the AM-OM sample and may cause a negative effect. Experimental Setup The lap shear specimens were placed under tensile load using a universal frame (313 Universal Frame, Test Resources) following the guidance from ASTM __, shown in Figure 5.4.4.(a). A reduced loading rate of 2.0 mm/min was performed instead of the recommended 13 mm/min due to matching the strain rate best for the polymer composite within the AM-OM sample. An out-of-plane displacement was occurring during testing which was the cause of premature failing due to peeling. Additional fixturing were 35 | P age clamped to each specimen to preserve alignment during testing, shown in Figure 5.4.4.(b-c). Figure 5.4.4: Out-of-plane bending occurred and caused premature failure. Additional stiffening fixtures were added to the specimen to reduce this occurrence. It is well understood the interface between adhesive and substrate is critical to optimized. Initial testing, using moderate sanding (100 grit sandpaper) on all surfaces the adhesive would be in contact, displayed poor interface failures between the adhesive and steel substrate tab. Therefore, an interfacial study was necessary. Three surface preparation options for the steel tab material were explored; (1) the initial 100 grit sandpaper, (2) grinding wheel, and (3) a slotted channel which the AM-OM samples would set in and allow mechanical influence (along with grinding wheel abrasive post-machining), shown in Figure 5.4.5. Figure 5.4.5: Initial failure modes showed lack of interfacial adhesion between the adhesive and steel tab substrate. Three (a) surface preparation options were explored including (1) 100 grit sandpaper, (2) grinding wheel, and (3) a slotted channel along with grinding wheel abrasive post-machining. The (b) slotted channel outline can be seen. 36 | P age Shear Testing Results The interface study results are displayed in Figure 5.4.7 and describe a 77% improvement when using the grinding wheel abrasive from moderate sanding as the surface roughness improved. There was a 24% reduction in lap shear strength when introducing the slotted geometry, but it is believed this is caused by out-of-plane motion which caused a premature peeling affect. Therefore, additional support was added to preserve the alignment resulting in a 227% increase in the lap shear strength response. Even with the increase in shear strength, the failure modes occurred between adhesive and AM-OM sample interface and not within the AM-OM sample itself. Fig.5.4.6.
